investigations.name: bird-01-transport-process
investigations.description:
Splits the monolithic BiRDReactorProcess into a shared transport module
plus a MonodCellProcess (the extracted biomass/consumption term) and two
reactor consumers. BiRDTransportProcess owns no biomass equation and no
substrate consumption; it emits only the gas–liquid transport
contribution at the shared dissolved-species stores, leaving growth and
exchange to the coupled cell engine. The extracted MonodCellProcess
conforms to the cell-side interface contract and doubles as the trivial
cell-side fixture for the coupled studies (Phases 2–4).

Verification is per-edge and regression-oriented: the new process emits
zero biomass delta, correct kLa-driven O2 transport, zero glucose
transport, and symmetric CO2 stripping; the retained BiRDReactorProcess
(transport + MonodCellProcess) reproduces pre-refactor trajectories; and
the MonodCellProcess passes the cell-side contract conformance fixture.
investigations.title: Transport-process split
investigations.objective:
Can the gas–liquid transport physics be extracted into a shared module
and exposed as a biomass-as-input BiRDTransportProcess that emits only
the transport contribution, while the standalone BiRDReactorProcess (now
transport + an extracted MonodCellProcess) keeps its pre-refactor
behavior?
investigations.claim: The gas-liquid transport physics is cleanly extracted: the standalone BiRDReactorProcess reproduces the pre-refactor trajectories, while the transport-only BiRDTransportProcess emits zero biomass delta, kLa-driven O2 transport, zero glucose transport, and symmetric CO2 stripping - biomass ownership sits entirely with the cell engine.

investigations.name: bird-02-closed-loop-liveness
investigations.description:
This is the integration test the single-process reactor cannot provide:
the reactor→cell direction only fires when biomass is dense enough to
perturb reactor state. The Phase-1 MonodCellProcess supplies biomass and
an O2 consumption flux under the cell-side contract; a constant scale
factor on a representative biomass is sufficient here — no growth dynamics
are needed to establish liveness.

Distinct from bird-01's per-edge unit checks, this study exercises the
composed loop end-to-end and asserts mass-balance closure across the two
processes' contributions at the shared dissolved-O2 store.
investigations.title: Closed-loop liveness
investigations.objective:
When BiRDTransportProcess is coupled to the Phase-1 MonodCellProcess at a
static high biomass density, does the reactor→cell feedback fire —
dissolved O2 dropping below saturation as consumption outpaces transport —
with O2 mass balance closing across cell and reactor contributions?
investigations.claim: Coupling the transport process to the Monod cell at high biomass fires the reactor->cell feedback - dissolved O2 drops below air saturation as consumption outpaces transport - and recovers toward saturation when biomass is removed; the O2 mass balance closes.

investigations.name: bird-03-coupling-interval
investigations.description:
The BiRD coupling interval is currently fixed. This study parameterizes it
and characterizes convergence, resolving the coupler-timestep-tunability
question raised by v2ecoli mbp-03. Builds on the live coupled loop from
bird-02.
investigations.title: Coupling-interval convergence
investigations.objective:
Can the reactor coupling/update interval be exposed as a tunable parameter,
and does the coupled trajectory converge as the interval decreases?
investigations.claim: The reactor coupling/update interval is a tunable parameter, and the coupled trajectory converges as the interval decreases (dt -> 0).

investigations.name: bird-04-reactor-geometry
investigations.description:
The high-cell-density benchmark uses a stirred-tank vessel; the current
transport form assumes bubble-column. This study adds a configurable
geometry and validates the stirred-tank kLa against literature, resolving
the reactor-geometry-for-benchmark question from mbp-03. Builds on the
coupled loop established in bird-02.
investigations.title: Reactor geometry & axial structure
investigations.objective:
Can the reactor support a stirred-tank kLa correlation (the benchmark
geometry) alongside the bubble-column form, selectable by configuration?
investigations.claim: The reactor supports a stirred-tank (Van't Riet) kLa correlation alongside the bubble-column (Higbie) form, selectable by configuration; a depth-resolved 1D column additionally resolves the axial O2/biomass structure the 0D model cannot express.
